title: Build a training sandbox or use system simulations?
summary: Compare a training sandbox with system simulations by examining workflow fidelity, maintenance effort and the practice your learners need.
body_markdown:
A sandbox and a simulation can both provide practice, but they solve different parts of the problem. Choose based on what the learner needs to do and what your team can maintain.


## Define the fidelity you need


List the decisions and actions that matter. Does a learner need to find an account, interpret a policy and complete a transaction? Does the exercise also need a customer conversation? Separate these requirements from a desire to replicate every screen and backend behaviour.


## Understand what a sandbox does well


A native sandbox can provide access to real application behaviour and integrations without changing production. It may be the right choice for technical testing or broad exploration. Check whether it also provides suitable training records, resettable exercises, customer interaction and assessment.


## Understand what a simulation needs to prove


A focused simulation can let people rehearse a defined workflow and receive feedback. Ask to see the paths a learner can take, what happens after a mistake and which parts are simplified. Confirm your own workflow rather than assuming support for every internal system.


## Include maintenance in the comparison


Account for initial configuration, test data, access, resets and updates when production changes. Assign an owner to each task. A low initial build cost can hide ongoing work; a vendor proposal should make scope, review responsibilities and update effort clear too.


## Test one representative task


Have a trainer and an experienced representative try the same workflow. Ask whether the practice teaches a useful behaviour and whether the environment can support your programme. Solidroad system simulations are worth evaluating when you need practice in tools alongside the conversation, rather than a full application test environment.
